explainer_reply:
The activations here are uniformly low (mostly 2–4) and the highlighted tokens are highly heterogeneous: punctuation marks, newlines, common function words ("to", "of", "in", "were"), subword fragments of names ("rz", "us", "arr", "ension"), and occasional content words. The surrounding contexts are dominated by expository prose—frequently religious/biblical discussion (Jesus, the Gospels, the woman of Samaria, priests) and ancient Roman history (Raeti, Augustus, Tiberius)—plus some physics quiz formatting. No consistent lexical, syntactic, or semantic feature unites the marked tokens; the neuron appears to fire weakly and diffusely on assorted mid-sentence tokens rather than selectively.

[EXPLANATION]: Weak, non-selective firing on assorted mid-sentence tokens (function words, punctuation, name fragments) within expository prose, often religious or historical text; no clear consistent pattern.
